trophies.name: The Rust Belt Lantern
trophies.obj: A brakeman’s railroad lantern, red glass, from the old freight line that ran Ann Arbor to Columbus.
trophies.rule: Whoever holds it hangs it in the tunnel. It travels lit.

trophies.name: The Sunset Compass
trophies.obj: A brass surveyor’s compass mounted on a slab of Pasadena oak; the needle is engraved with both schools’ colours.
trophies.rule: Eleven miles apart. The holder decides which way the needle points.

trophies.name: The Red River Rail Spike
trophies.obj: A foot-long iron spike from a rail bridge over the Red River, set upright in a block of red granite.
trophies.rule: The loser has to drive the next one.

trophies.name: The Sunshine Anchor
trophies.obj: A cast-iron boat anchor hauled out of the Suwannee, painted half garnet, half orange and blue.
trophies.rule: Too heavy to lift in celebration. Somebody always tries.

trophies.name: The Saint Marys Ferry Bell
trophies.obj: The bronze bell off a ferry that crossed the Saint Marys River, the water that splits Florida from Georgia.
trophies.rule: Rung once for every goal of the winning margin.

trophies.name: The Gulf Coast Gavel
trophies.obj: A judge’s gavel turned from a live-oak branch, with the scores of every meeting burned into the handle.
trophies.rule: A draw is a hung jury. The gavel stays where it is.

trophies.name: The Caprock Lamp
trophies.obj: A miner’s carbide lamp found on the Llano Estacado, on a base of Lubbock red clay and Austin limestone.
trophies.rule: The holder keeps it burning until the next meeting.

trophies.name: The Coast-to-Coast Clock
trophies.obj: A two-faced station clock: one face on Pacific time, one on Eastern. Only the holder’s face is wound.
trophies.rule: The loser’s face stops at the final whistle.

trophies.name: The Peninsula Shield
trophies.obj: A hammered copper shield shaped like the state of Florida, with Coral Gables and Tallahassee picked out in brass.
trophies.rule: Hung above the holder’s dressing-room door, facing out.

trophies.name: The Tobacco Road Milestone
trophies.obj: A granite mile-marker from the road between Chapel Hill and Durham: “DURHAM 8” on one side, “CHAPEL HILL 8” on the other.
trophies.rule: It faces the holder’s town. It has not been turned around.

odds.note: Season 3 after the opening fortnight: 20,000 simulations of the 427 remaining fixtures read from the save. June’s pre-season ratings are the prior, the 35 games played are the update, weighted by games played; everything shrunk 20% towards the average.

timeline.note: Posts are invented. Only fictional players (newgens) and Touchline's own fictional staff post here. Real players never do. Every scoreline and goal referenced is from the save.

posts.text: Season 3, No. 1 is out. Michigan 21–2 in three games, Florida State top with four wins, the odds re-run: Michigan 46%, Georgia 23%, Florida State 14%. And the first update on all sixteen storylines.
Clemson 0, Michigan 9. Twenty-one scored, two conceded. I asked for a goalkeeper. They sent an attack. I’ll take it.
First goal of the season. Seven assists too, if anyone’s counting. I am.
Georgia: 9 scored in 3. Last season: 4.02 a game. The pace is the story and the pace is down a goal. Three wins from three, mind.
Three at Notre Dame. 8, 23, 48. Sixteen years old and I’m not sleeping tonight.
Two games, two clean sheets. 9–0 today. Columbus is fine. 🧤

replies.text: The structure question is still open. The goalkeeper question has started well.

posts.text: First goal for the Canes. 5–2. Needed that, all of us did.
Miami 0, LSU 1. The eleven was eleventh on ability and it played like it. The model had them third. One of us is wrong and it isn’t the one who watched.
Opening day: 62 goals in eleven games. Oklahoma 8–0 TCU with five from Jackson Conway, the first a penalty inside a minute. Georgia 3–2 at North Carolina, Robledo at 90. Michigan 6–1 Florida.
Season 3 preview is out. 20,000 simulations: Georgia 34%, Michigan 21%, Miami 20%. Power rankings: Michigan first. Opening day, August 19: North Carolina v Georgia.
Our model says Georgia. Our rankings say Michigan. I say whoever finds a goalkeeper first.
Sixteen and first choice. Pre-season can’t come soon enough. 🧤
Torres, Damus, Pellegrini, Haji. Thank you for everything. Now it’s our turn to carry it.
Gold Cup: U.S.A. 3–0 Trinidad & Tobago. De la Fuente 2, Dike. Nine of the eleven starters have played in the Sixteen.
Seventeen. Someone asked me about ceilings in May. Still later. Back in Austin soon.
First pre-season with the Canes coming up. Been waiting for this since March.
Draft 23 by the numbers: picks landed 7.4 slots from our board on average. Last year it was 2.2.
U.S.A. 6–0 Portugal. World champions at Under-20 level for the first time. Seven wins from seven.
Lottery night. Seattle win it and pick first at their own draft on June 20. The host winning was a 1-in-21 shot. Inter Miami, 14th in the table, jump to second.
Three for my country. Colombia Wednesday. 🇺🇸
Georgia are champions. 10–1 at TCU, 96 points, three clear of Michigan. With the Youth League and the Cotton Bowl, that is the treble.
Duke went to Clemson on the last day, won 3–1, finished level on points and went down anyway. Seven goals of difference. I have no notes.
Second in the league and the Rose Bowl. Proud of this group. Year one done. 〽️
Bowl finals night. Cotton: LSU 3–4 Georgia, Robledo hat-trick. Rose: Michigan 3–2 Ohio State, Balogun twice. Fiesta: Oklahoma 3–1 Texas Tech.
Two finals, two goals, two trophies. Don’t wake me up.
Scored in a final and lost it. That one is going to stay with me. We’ll be back.
Georgia win the FIFA Youth League. 3–1 against North Carolina: Will Sands, Damus, and a 16-year-old in added time.
Two at Oklahoma, 5–3. Fifth place is in our hands now. 🐘
Ten past Oregon to finish the season. Thanks for everything, Tallahassee. Back in August.

April, read straight from the save. Georgia 90, Texas 88, Michigan 87, Oklahoma and Alabama 86, Miami 84. Two games left, five Youth League places. The game that matters most on the real fixtures: Miami v Texas, May 27.
Draft 23 has a home. Seattle, Tuesday, June 20. 84 graduates, 21 clubs, four full rounds.
Redrafting the Class of 2022 on ability now: McKennie first, Pulisic second, Adams third. Biggest climb among the first two rounds: Davide Bove, 24th to 13th.
Alabama beat Michigan 4–0 and Georgia 2–0 in the same month and are FIFTH. This league.
Two today. Would trade both for the win. 〽️
First goal. Thank you Ann Arbor.
Scored in the 11 at TCU this month. 182 league goals with two to play and we still need help.
Miami. Right back. Let’s work.
Westwood 💙💛 can’t wait to start
Texas Tech: 15 points from 15 in April, and next year the best returning XI in the league on current ability. Eighth this year.

March, read straight from the save. Michigan 80, Georgia 80, Texas 79, seven games each to play. Title odds on the real fixtures: Georgia 59%, Michigan 25%, Texas 13%. And 51 new players at the Sixteen.
Intake by school, the Almanac formula: Michigan first, Notre Dame second, Ohio State third. Michigan’s is a one-man score until you see Sean O’Shea at 153.
80 minutes and an assist. Lots to work on. Go Blue 〽️
Scored after five minutes and Florida scored twice by seven. Won 5–2. One point behind with seven to go.
New city, new badge. Washington, let’s go.

92nd minute in Baton Rouge. Bus is loud tonight.
